title: Set operations treat NULLs as equal; there is no `INTERSECT ALL`
verdict: `UNION`, `INTERSECT`, `EXCEPT`/`MINUS`; the `ALL` forms are unsupported but `UNION ALL`
description: `UNION` keeps one NULL; `INTERSECT` keeps a NULL both sides have; `EXCEPT` and `MINUS` are one. `INTERSECT ALL` and `EXCEPT ALL` raise `Unsupported feature`. NaN and -0.0 meet their equals (`INTERSECT` keeps the left side's -0.0). A `UNION ALL` of `NUMBER`s and a `FLOAT` is `FLOAT`.
reference: Set operations with NULLs equal, `ALL` forms by multiplicity. sverify's SQL writes `UNION ALL` and grouping, never `INTERSECT` or `EXCEPT`.

provenance.checked_by: sverify_dev.probe_snowflake through the Snowflake CLI (Snowflake characterization session)

evidence.sql: SELECT x FROM (VALUES (1), (1), (2), (NULL), (NULL)) AS s(x) UNION SELECT x FROM (VALUES (1), (NULL), (3)) AS s(x) ORDER BY x

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_snowflake` runs each query through `snow sql` (Snowflake CLI 3.32.1) on an X-Small warehouse, Snowflake 10.40.102, with the session's `TIMEZONE` set to UTC and `USE_CACHED_RESULT` off; every other parameter is the account's default, recorded in the header of probes.json (`WEEK_START` 0, `WEEK_OF_YEAR_POLICY` 0, `DEFAULT_NULL_ORDERING` LAST, `TIMESTAMP_TYPE_MAPPING` TIMESTAMP_NTZ). The inputs are literal `VALUES`, except the `sample-*` probes, which read TPC-H's LINEITEM (6,001,215 rows) in SNOWFLAKE_SAMPLE_DATA.
